papers.title_in_file: Reducing the Quantum Many-electron Problem to Two Electrons with Machine Learning
papers.what_it_is: A classical convolutional neural network predicts a correlation temperature that fixes geminal occupations and so molecular energies for hydrocarbons.

assertions.value: The authors report that a convolutional neural network trained on hydrocarbons with 2-7 carbon atoms predicts the energies of octane isomers and of hydrocarbons with 8-15 carbons.
quotes: By training on hydrocarbon isomers with only 2-7 carbon atoms, we are able to predict the energies for isomers of octane as well as hydrocarbons with 8-15 carbons.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on one molecule family.

assertions.value: The authors state that the predicted CASSCF energies show good agreement with the actual CASSCF energies, and that the error increases slightly as system size increases.
assertions.anchor: Results, Energetic Predictions for Large Hydrocarbon, p.4
quotes: the predicted CASSCF energies (green circles) show good agreement with the actual CASSCF energies (black boxes)
Although there is a slight increase in the error as system size is increased
assertions.certainty_reason: Qualitative reading of plotted energies from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The agreement is stated qualitatively; no numeric error is given in the text.

assertions.value: The authors state that the hydrocarbons used for training and testing do not show large degrees of correlation, and that application to highly-correlated systems is future work.
quotes: do not demonstrate large degrees of correlation
Application of our machine-learning reduced density matrix approach to highly-correlated systems is a future direction of this research.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its scope and limit.

papers.title_in_file: Advancements and Challenges in Quantum Machine Learning for Medical Image Classification: A Comprehensive Review
papers.what_it_is: A short review of quantum machine learning studies on medical image classification, covering QCNN, VQC and QSVM work.

assertions.value: The authors state that their review searched IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar and arXiv and was limited to publications from the past two years up to 2024.
quotes: A systematic search is conducted in prominent databases including IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar, and arXiv.
The search is limited to publications from the past two years up to 2024
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own scope.

assertions.value: The authors report, citing R V et al., that a QKSVM achieved 83.33% accuracy on a simulator and 82.8% on the AspenM3 quantum processing unit for DBT image classification.
quotes: QKSVM achieved 83.33% accuracy on a simulator, slightly higher than 82.8% on the AspenM3 quantum processing unit
assertions.certainty_reason: A cited result reported second hand in a review.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum models have proven successful in binary classification, while their performance in complicated multiclass classification remains unexplored.
quotes: While several quantum models have proven successful in binary classification tasks, their performance in complicated multiclass classification contexts remains unexplored.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim in a review, without a systematic count shown in the text.
assertions.reader_inference: This sits beside Section 4, which cites multiclass QCNN and VQC studies, so the claim is in tension with the paper's own text.

assertions.value: The authors state that applying QML on real hardware faces quantum noise, a limited number of available qubits and high error rates in NISQ devices.
assertions.anchor: 5 Real-world applications using quantum hardware, p.13
quotes: including quantum noise, a limited number of available qubits, and high error rates inherent in noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's general statement, not a measured result.

papers.title_in_file: Variational quantum eigensolver with linear depth problem-inspired ansatz for solving portfolio optimization in finance
papers.what_it_is: Origin Quantum authors design two Dicke-state VQE ansatze for portfolio optimization and run them on a superconducting quantum computer.

assertions.value: The authors report portfolio optimization runs on a superconducting quantum computer for up to 55 qubits (assets), using a hybrid distributed computing scheme.
quotes: In this paper, we have achieved the common portfolio optimizations using a superconducting computer for up to 55 qubits (assets)
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study; authors are affiliated with the hardware vendor.
assertions.reader_inference: The workload is classical portfolio optimization, so this is a quantum computing result, not a machine learning one.

assertions.value: The authors state that they implemented hybrid distributed computing experiments on a superconducting quantum computer with up to 55 qubits.
quotes: we successfully implement the HDC experiments on a superconducting quantum computer with up to 55 qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' interpretation of simulation and one hardware experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that they applied only the simplest error mitigation method, measurement error mitigation, and that the error-prone nature of NISQ computers limits capability further.
quotes: we just applied the simplest quantum error mitigation method, i.e. quantum measurement error mitigation.
the error-prone issue of NISQ computers limits their capability further
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own limits.

assertions.value: The authors state that ergodically searching the partitioned subspaces may not be efficient in some cases, so obtaining potential quantum advantage is not assured.
quotes: to obtain potential quantum advantages, ergodically searching these subspaces may not be efficient in some cases
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own limits.

papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction and conclusions heading; skimmed the rest.
papers.what_it_is: A mathematics paper on recovering a potential on a quantum tree graph (a differential-equation graph) from a Weyl matrix.
papers.why_not: Quantum graphs here are metric graphs carrying Sturm-Liouville equations. The paper has no link to quantum computing, quantum machine learning, machine learning, finance or evaluation method.

papers.title_in_file: A general framework for active space embedding methods: applications in quantum computing
papers.what_it_is: A hybrid quantum-classical embedding framework in CP2K, tested on the oxygen vacancy in MgO with VQE and qEOM.

assertions.value: The authors state that they developed a general framework for hybrid quantum-classical embedding based on an orbital space separation of fragment and environment, and demonstrated it on the neutral oxygen vacancy in MgO using VQE and qEOM.
assertions.anchor: Abstract and V. Conclusions, pp.1 and 11
quotes: We developed a general framework for hybrid quantum-classical computing of molecular and periodic embedding approaches based on an orbital space separation of the fragment and environment degrees of freedom.
the low-lying spectrum of the embedded fragment Hamiltonian has been calculated by VQE and qEOM, in combination with the q-UCCSD ansatz
assertions.certainty_reason: One system studied by one group.

assertions.value: The authors report a predicted absorption peak of 5.78 eV that overestimates the experimental result by 0.75 eV, and a predicted emission of 2.44 eV against an experimental signal at 2.3 eV.
quotes: Our calculations for the absorption spectrum predict a peak at 5.78 eV, a value that overestimates the experimental result by 0.75 eV
the predicted PL emission of 2.44 eV from the
experimentally measured signal at 2.3 eV
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result for one defect in one material.

assertions.value: The authors state that the accuracy for absorption leaves room for improvement and that the excellent agreement for emission is helped by favorable error compensation.
quotes: While the accuracy of the method for the absorption leaves room for improvement, and the excellent agreement for the emission is certainly helped by favorable error compensation
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own limits.

papers.title_in_file: A Framework for Curriculum Transformation in Quantum Information Science and Technology Education
papers.what_it_is: A decision-tree framework (QCTF) for designing quantum information science and technology curricula, illustrated with quantum teleportation.

assertions.value: The authors state that the Quantum Curriculum Transformation Framework has four steps: choose a topic, choose targeted skills, choose a learning goal and choose a teaching approach.
quotes: The Quantum Curriculum Transformation Framework (QCTF) consists of four steps: 1. choose a topic, 2. choose one or more targeted skills, 3. choose a learning goal and 4. choose a teaching approach that achieves this goal.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own design.

assertions.value: The authors state that many new educational courses and university programs are needed to prepare a workforce for the developing quantum industry.
quotes: many new educational courses and university programs are needed in order to prepare a workforce for the developing industry
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim, with no data shown in the abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that the framework needs future testing and refinement, and describe it as a guiding structure.
assertions.anchor: Abstract and 8. Outlook and Discussion, pp.1 and 23
quotes: with future testing and refinement it will form a basis for further research in the didactics of QIST
We emphasise that the framework is a guiding structure
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own status and limit.

papers.what_it_is: A hybrid variational algorithm that appends a classical tensor-network unitary to a shallow parametrized quantum circuit.

assertions.value: The authors state that the tensor-network-assisted circuits increase expressivity without requiring a physically deeper circuit.
quotes: which concatenate a classical tensor-network operator with a quantum circuit to effectively increase the circuit's expressivity without requiring a physically deeper circuit
assertions.certainty_reason: Design statement in the abstract; support is numerical simulation.

assertions.value: The authors report that on two-dimensional Ising models and one-dimensional time-crystal Hamiltonian models with up to 16 qubits, the approach consistently outperforms conventional methods using shallow quantum circuits.
quotes: We apply our method to two-dimensional Ising models and one-dimensional timecrystal Hamiltonian models with up to 16 qubits and demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms conventional methods using shallow quantum circuits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation of small systems from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The tested size is at most 16 qubits, so the claim is not shown for larger systems.

assertions.value: The authors state that their numerical experiments showed the framework is robust to noise.
quotes: Our numerical experiments also showed that the proposed framework is robust to noise
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated noise in one study.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Programming of the Satisfiability Problem with Rydberg Atom Graphs
papers.what_it_is: An experiment encoding 3-SAT instances as maximum independent set problems on Rydberg atom graphs and reading out many-body ground states.

assertions.value: The authors state that they present an experiment using Rydberg atoms to program the 3-SAT problem through blockade interactions and obtain many-body ground states to determine satisfiability.
quotes: Here an experiment is presented to demonstrate the use of Rydberg atoms to solve
Boolean expressions of the 3-SAT problem are programmed with the blockade interactions of Rydberg atom graphs and their many-body ground states are experimentally obtained
assertions.certainty_reason: Small-instance experiment from one group.

assertions.value: The authors report an estimated ground state fidelity of 81% for the experimental 2D graph, improved to 90% for an alternative more symmetric graph, in simulated quasi-adiabatic evolution.
quotes: the fidelity is estimated to be 81%, due to the contribution of long-range residual Rydberg interactions among atoms spaced beyond the Rydberg blockade radius
after the same quasi-adiabatic evolution is improved to 90%
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical estimate for one instance family.

assertions.value: The authors state that it is difficult to conclude the technical limits of the still-nascent Rydberg atom technology.
quotes: While it is difficult to conclude the technical limits of this still-nascent Rydberg atom technology
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own limits.
assertions.reader_inference: The body of the paper also estimates a one-week run for a large instance; that figure was left out because its quote did not pass the checker.
